nodes.name: The underlying set of a cusp
nodes.statement: The underlying set of a cusp is defined as the quotient of R times left] a, + infty right[ by the action of the translation left( x,y right) mapsto left( x+1, y right), or alternatively as the product S^1 times left] a, + infty right[, endowed with the Poincaré metric \[ lll ds^2_hyp & = & fracdx^2 + dy^2y^2 . \] Using the coordinate z = exp left( 2 i pi left( x+iy right) right), a cusp can also be seen as a punctured disk of radius varepsilon =exp left( - 2 pi a right), whose center corresponds to the singularity.

                \end{array} , \]
            
            \noindent called the Chern Laplacian with Dirichlet boundary conditions.

\label{LemmaSpectralCountingLineBundle}

nodes.statement: First, we note that the result is automatic if the line bundle L is trivial. Let us therefore assume this is not the case, i.e. that alpha is non-zero. The pseudo-Laplacian Delta_L,0 is then the Chern Laplacian Delta_L, as specified in definition . Since chi having finite order is equivalent to the rationality of alpha, we have n alpha in Z. In this proof, we identify any section of L to a function psi : R times left] a, + infty right[ longrightarrow C which satisfies psi left( x+1, y right) = e^2 i pi alpha psi left( x, y right). Such a function is n-periodic in the first variable, and the map \[ cccllll f & : & C^infty left( S^1 times left] a, +infty right[, L right) & longrightarrow & multicolumn3lC^infty left( S^1 times left] fracan, +infty right[ right) \\[0.5em] && psi & longmapsto & left( x, y right) & longmapsto & psi left( nx, ny right) \] is an injection from the space of smooth sections of L into the space of smooth functions (i.e. smooth sections of the trivial line bundle), which commutes with the Chern Laplacians. For any smooth section psi of L, and any y > a/n, we have \[ lllllll scriptstyle int_0^1 \; f left( psi right) left( x, y right) \; dx & scriptstyle = & scriptstyle int_0^1 \; psi left( nx, ny right) \; dx & scriptstyle = & scriptstyle frac1n sumlimits_j=0^n-1 left( e^2ipi alpha right)^j int_0^1 \; psi left( x, ny right) \; dx & scriptstyle = & scriptstyle 0, \] Thus f takes values in the space of smooth sections with vanishing constant Fourier coefficient. Now, we have \[ lll scriptstyle int_a/n^+ infty \; int_0^1 \; left( Delta f left( psi right) right) left( x, y right) overlinef left( psi right) left( x, y right) \; fracdx \, dyy^2 & scriptstyle = & scriptstyle int_a/n^+ infty \; int_0^1 \; left( Delta_L psi right) left( nx, ny right) overlinepsi left( nx, ny right) \; fracdx \, dyy^2 \\[0.8em] & = & scriptstyle n int_a^+ infty \; int_0^1 \; left( Delta_L psi right) left( x, y right) overlinepsi left( x, y right) \; fracdx \, dyy^2. \] Similarly, we have \[ lll int_a/n^+ infty \; int_0^1 \; f left( psi right) left( x, y right) overlinef left( psi right) left( x, y right) \; fracdx \, dyy^2 & = & n int_a^+ infty \; int_0^1 \; psi left( x, y right) overlinepsi left( x, y right) \; fracdx \, dyy^2. \] Taking the quotient of these two integrals, assuming psi is non-zero, we get lll fracoverlineQ_Delta left( f left( psi right), f left( psi right) right)left< f left( psi right), f left( psi right) right> & = & fracoverlineQ_Delta_L left( psi, psi right)left< psi, psi right>. The map f then extends into \[ lllll f & : & L^2_1,Dir left( R times left] a, + infty right[, L right) & longrightarrow & L^2_1,Dir left( R times left] a, + infty right[ right)_0 , \] Furthermore, equality remains valid for this continuation. This allows us to compare the spectral quantities mu_n and mu_n left( Delta_L right), as we have \[ lll multicolumn3linflimits_f left( psi_1 right), dots, f left( psi_k right) sup left \ fracoverlineQ_Delta left( f left( psi right), f left( psi right) right)left< f left( psi right), f left( psi right) right>, \; f left( psi right) in span left( f left( psi_1 right), dots, f left( psi_k right) right), \; f left( psi right) neq 0 right \ \\[1em] & leqslant & inflimits_psi_1, dots, psi_k sup left \ fracoverlineQ_Delta_L left( psi, psi right)left< psi, psi right>, \; psi in span left( psi_1, dots, psi_k right), \; psi neq 0 right \. \] Replacing the lower bound on the left-hand side by one with respect to k elements in the L_1^2 space, instead of just the image of f, we get \[ lll mu_k left( a/n right) & leqslant & mu_k left( L right) . \] We can now use the definition of the spectral counting functions, and get the result.

nodes.statement: Consider a real number lambda > 0. Using lemma , we have \[ lll N left( Delta_L,0, lambda right) & leqslant & N_a/n left( lambda right) . \] Extending by 0 gives an injection \[ lll L_1, Dir^2 left( S^1 times left] a, +infty right[ right)_0 & hookrightarrow & L_1, Dir^2 left( S^1 times left] fracan, +infty right[ right)_0, \] which yields N_a/n left( lambda right) leqslant N_a left( lambda right), using proposition . We further have \[ lllll N_a left( lambda right) & = & N left( Delta^D_left] a, + infty right[, lambda right) & leqslant & N left( Delta^N_left] a, + infty right[, lambda right) , \] since operators for the Dirichlet boundary condition and the Neumann one can be compared using lemma . The idea presented in by Colin de Verdière can be used to break apart the interval left] a, +infty right[, which yields, for a fixed delta > 0, \[ lll N left( Delta^N_left] a, + infty right[, lambda right) & leqslant & sumlimits_k=0^ell - 1 \; N left( Delta^N_left] a+k delta, a+left( k+1 right) delta right[, lambda right) + N left( Delta^N_left] a + ell, + infty right[, lambda right) \] after having applied lemma inductively. Consider a real number $\lambda > 0$. Using lemma \ref{LemmaSpectralCountingLineBundle}, we have
            
            \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                    N \left( \Delta_{L,0}, \lambda \right) & \leqslant & N_{a/n} \left( \lambda \right)
                \end{array} . \]
                
            \noindent Extending by $0$ gives an injection
            
            
            \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                    L_{1, \mathrm{Dir}}^2 \left( S^1 \times \left] a, +\infty \right[ \right)_0 & \hookrightarrow & L_{1, \mathrm{Dir}}^2 \left( S^1 \times \left] \frac{a}{n}, +\infty \right[ \right)_0,
                \end{array} \]
            
            \noindent which yields $N_{a/n} \left( \lambda \right) \leqslant N_a \left( \lambda \right)$, using proposition \ref{PropSpectralCountingOrderRelation}. We further have
            
            \[ \begin{array}{lllll}
                    N_a \left( \lambda \right) & = & N \left( \Delta^D_{\left] a, + \infty \right[}, \lambda \right) & \leqslant & N \left( \Delta^N_{\left] a, + \infty \right[}, \lambda \right)
                \end{array} , \]
            
            \noindent since operators for the Dirichlet boundary condition and the Neumann one can be compared using lemma \ref{LemDNBracketing}. The idea presented in \cite[Thm 6]{MR699488} by Colin de Verdière can be used to break apart the interval $\left] a, +\infty \right[$, which yields, for a fixed $\delta > 0$,
            
            \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                    N \left( \Delta^N_{\left] a, + \infty \right[}, \lambda \right) & \leqslant & \sum\limits_{k=0}^{\ell - 1} \; N \left( \Delta^N_{\left] a+k \delta, a+\left( k+1 \right) \delta \right[}, \lambda \right) + N \left( \Delta^N_{\left] a + \ell, + \infty \right[}, \lambda \right)
                \end{array} \]
            
            \noindent after having applied lemma \ref{LemNeumannBreakingInterval} inductively. We now note that lemma \ref{LemmaSpectralCountingSchrinkingCusp} gives us an integer $\ell_a$, depending on $a$ in an unknown manner, such that we have
            
            \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                     N \left( \Delta^N_{\left] a + \ell, + \infty \right[}, \lambda \right) & = & 0
                \end{array} \]
            
            \noindent for any integer $\ell \geqslant \ell_a$. For such integers, we have
            
            \[ \begin{array}{llllll}
                    N \left( \Delta^N_{\left] a, + \infty \right[}, \lambda \right) & \leqslant & \sum\limits_{k=0}^{\ell - 1} \; N \left( \Delta^N_{\left] a+k \delta, a+\left( k+1 \right) \delta \right[}, \lambda \right) \\[1em]
                    
                    & \leqslant & \sum\limits_{k=0}^{+ \infty} \; N \left( \Delta^N_{\left] a+k \delta, a+\left( k+1 \right) \delta \right[}, \lambda \right) \\[1em]
                    
                    & \leqslant & \sum\limits_{k=0}^{+ \infty} \; N \left( \Delta^N_{\left] a+k \delta, a+\left( k+1 \right) \delta \right[}, \frac{\lambda}{\left( a + k \delta \right)^2} \right) & \text{by lemma \ref{LemmaNeumannLaplacianPoincaréEuclidean}}.
                \end{array} \]
            
            \noindent The inequality formed by the first and last term above does not depend on $\ell$, and thus removes the problem of not understanding how $\ell_a$ varies with respect to $a$. The added terms do not play much of a role, since lemma \ref{LemmaSpectralCountingNeumannEuclidean} says we have
            
            \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                    N \left( \Delta^N_{\left] a+k \delta, a+\left( k+1 \right) \delta \right[}, \frac{\lambda}{\left( a + k \delta \right)^2} \right) & = & 0
                \end{array} \]
            
            \noindent if the inequality $\lambda < 4 \pi^2 \left( a + k \delta \right)^2$ is satisfied. Let us set
            
            \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                    k_a & = & \left \lfloor \frac{1}{\delta} \left[ \frac{1}{2\pi} \sqrt{\lambda} - a \right] \right \rfloor
                \end{array} , \]
            
            \noindent where $\left \lfloor x \right \rfloor$ denotes the largest integer smaller than $x$. We get
            
            \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                    N \left( \Delta^N_{\left] a, + \infty \right[}, \lambda \right) & \leqslant & \sum\limits_{k=0}^{k_a} \; N \left( \Delta^N_{\left] a+k \delta, a+\left( k+1 \right) \delta \right[}, \frac{\lambda}{\left( a + k \delta \right)^2} \right)
                \end{array} . \]
            
            \noindent We will now evaluate this term, using the method described in \cite[Thm 6]{MR699488}. Each term summed on the right-hand side above being evaluated in lemma \ref{LemmaSpectralCountingNeumannEuclidean}, we have
            
            \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                    N \left( \Delta^N_{\left] a, + \infty \right[}, \lambda \right) & \leqslant & \frac{\delta \lambda}{4 \pi} \sum\limits_{k=0}^{k_a} \; \frac{1}{\left( a + k \delta \right)^2} + \frac{1}{\pi} \sqrt{\lambda} \sum\limits_{k=0}^{k_a} \; \frac{1}{a + k \delta}
                \end{array} . \]
            
            \noindent Comparing series and integrals, we get
            
            \[ \begin{array}{lllll}
                    \frac{\delta \lambda}{4 \pi} \sum\limits_{k=0}^{k_a} \; \frac{1}{\left( a + k \delta \right)^2} & = & \multicolumn{3}{l}{\frac{\delta \lambda}{4 \pi a^2} + \frac{\lambda}{4 \pi} \sum\limits_{k=1}^{k_a} \; \int_{a+\left( k - 1 \right) \delta}^{a + k \delta} \; \frac{1}{\left( a + k \delta \right)^2} \; \mathrm{d}y} \\[1em]
                    
                    & \leqslant & \frac{\delta \lambda}{4 \pi a^2} + \frac{\lambda}{4 \pi} \sum\limits_{k=1}^{+ \infty} \; \int_{a+\left( k - 1 \right) \delta}^{a + k \delta} \; \frac{1}{y^2} \; \mathrm{d}y & = & \frac{\delta \lambda}{4 \pi a^2} + \frac{\lambda}{4 \pi a}
                \end{array} \]
            
            \noindent for the first term, and, similarly
            
            \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                    \frac{1}{\pi} \sqrt{\lambda} \sum\limits_{k=0}^{k_a} \; \frac{1}{a + k \delta} & = & \frac{1}{\pi} \sqrt{\lambda} \left[ \frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{\delta} \sum\limits_{k=1}^{k_a} \; \int_{a + \left( k-1 \right) \delta}^{a + k \delta} \; \frac{1}{a + k \delta} \mathrm{d}y \right] \\[1em]

                    & \leqslant & \frac{1}{\pi a} \sqrt{\lambda} + \frac{1}{2 \pi \delta} \sqrt{\lambda} \log \lambda.
                \end{array} \]
            
            \noindent Combining these results, we get
            
            \begin{equation}
            \label{IneqWeylLaw}
                \begin{array}{lll}
                    N \left( \Delta^N_{\left] a, + \infty \right[}, \lambda \right) & \leqslant & \frac{1}{\pi a} \sqrt{\lambda} + \frac{1}{4 \pi a} \left[ 1 + \frac{\delta}{a} \right] \lambda + \frac{1}{2 \pi \delta} \sqrt{\lambda} \log \lambda
                \end{array} .
            \end{equation}
            
            \noindent All these estimates put together yield
            
            \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                    N \left( \Delta_{L,0}, \lambda \right) & \leqslant & \frac{1}{4 \pi a} \left[ 5 + \frac{\delta}{a} \right] \lambda + \frac{1}{2 \pi \delta} \sqrt{\lambda} \log \lambda
                \end{array} \]
            
            \noindent for any $\lambda > 1$ by using the inequality $\sqrt{\lambda} < \lambda$. The theorem follows on $\left[ 1, + \infty \right[$ by using the fact that the function $\lambda \mapsto \lambda^{-1/2} \log \lambda$ is bounded on $\left[ 1, + \infty \right[$, and then on $\mathbb{R}_+^{\ast}$ by further adjusting the constant.

nodes.statement: Let us assume that we have alpha neq 0, since the other case is similar. For every integer k in Z, the zeros of nu mapsto K_i nu left( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right) are simple, and denoted by r_k,j. The argument principle then states that we have, for any k in Z, \[ lll sumlimits_j geqslant 1 left( frac14 + r_k,j^2 + mu right)^-s & = & frac12 i pi int_gamma_vartheta \; left( frac14 + r^2 + mu right)^-s fracpartialpartial r log K_ir left( 2 pi left vert k+alpha right vert a right) dr . \] Using the Weyl type law, in order to make sense of the various series, we get \[ lll zeta_L, mu left( s right) & = & frac12 i pi sumlimits_k in Z \; int_gamma_vartheta \; left( frac14 + r^2 + mu right)^-s fracpartialpartial r log K_ir left( 2 pi left vert k+alpha right vert a right) dr. \] The change of variable t = ir then gives the required formula.
nodes.raw_latex:
Let us assume that we have $\alpha \neq 0$, since the other case is similar. For every integer $k \in \mathbb{Z}$, the zeros of $\nu \mapsto K_{i \nu} \left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right)$ are simple, and denoted by $r_{k,j}$. The argument principle then states that we have, for any $k \in \mathbb{Z}$,
            
            \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                    \sum\limits_{j \geqslant 1} \left( \frac{1}{4} + r_{k,j}^2 + \mu \right)^{-s} & = & \frac{1}{2 i \pi} \int_{\gamma_{\vartheta}} \; \left( \frac{1}{4} + r^2 + \mu \right)^{-s} \frac{\partial}{\partial r} \log K_{ir} \left( 2 \pi \left \vert k+\alpha \right \vert a \right) \mathrm{d}r
                \end{array} . \]
            
            \noindent Using the Weyl type law, in order to make sense of the various series, we get
            
            \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                    \zeta_{L, \mu} \left( s \right) & = & \frac{1}{2 i \pi} \sum\limits_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} \; \int_{\gamma_{\vartheta}} \; \left( \frac{1}{4} + r^2 + \mu \right)^{-s} \frac{\partial}{\partial r} \log K_{ir} \left( 2 \pi \left \vert k+\alpha \right \vert a \right) \mathrm{d}r.
                \end{array} \]
            
            \noindent The change of variable $t = ir$ then gives the required formula.

The argument principle then states that we have, for any k in Z, \[ lll sumlimits_j geqslant 1 left( frac14 + r_k,j^2 + mu right)^-s & = & frac12 i pi int_gamma_vartheta \; left( frac14 + r^2 + mu right)^-s fracpartialpartial r log K_ir left( 2 pi left vert k+alpha right vert a right) dr . \] Using the Weyl type law, in order to make sense of the various series, we get \[ lll zeta_L, mu left( s right) & = & frac12 i pi sumlimits_k in Z \; int_gamma_vartheta \; left( frac14 + r^2 + mu right)^-s fracpartialpartial r log K_ir left( 2 pi left vert k+alpha right vert a right) dr. \] The change of variable t = ir then gives the required formula.

nodes.statement: We first note that the function F_mu,k has been defined so as to have \[ lllll F_mu,k left( pm sqrtfrac14+mu right) & = & F_mu,k' left( pm sqrtfrac14+mu right) & = & 0 . \] Since F_mu,k is holomorphic in t, it is of the form F_mu,k left( t right)= h_mu,k left( t^2 right), where h_mu,k is holomorphic and such that we have \[ lllll h_mu,k left( frac14+mu right) & = & h_mu,k' left( frac14+mu right) & = & 0 . \] The Taylor-Lagrange theorem then allows us to write \[ lllll F_mu,k left( t right) & = & h_mu,k left( t^2 right) & = & frac12 \, left( t^2 - left( frac14+mu right) right)^2 \; h_mu,k'' left( xi_mu,t^2 right) , \] where xi_mu,t is a real number with sqrt1/4 + mu leqslant xi_mu,t leqslant 2 left vert k right vert^delta sqrt1/4 + mu. Note that we do not know how xi_mu,t depends on mu, t, or k. By differentiating F_mu,k, we get \[ lllclll F_mu,k' left( t right) & = & 2t h_mu,k' left( t^2 right), & & F_mu,k'' left( t right) & = & 2 h_mu,k' left( t^2 right) + 4t^2 h_mu,k'' left( t^2 right) , \] and these two equalities can be combined to yield \[ lll h_mu,k'' left( t^2 right) & = & frac14t^2 \, F_mu,k'' left( t right) - frac14t^3 \, F_mu,k' left( t right) \\[0.5em] & = & frac14t^2 \, fracpartial^2partial t^2 log K_t left( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right) - frac14t^3 \, fracpartialpartial t log K_t left( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right) \] Therefore, we have \[ scalemath0.98lll F_mu,k left( t right) & = & left( t^2 - left( frac14+mu right) right)^2 left[ frac14xi_mu,t^2 \, fracpartial^2partial t^2_vert t \, = \, xi_mu,t log K_t left( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right) right. \\[1em] && - left. frac14xi_mu,t^3 \, fracpartialpartial t_vert t \, = \, xi_mu,t log K_t left( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right) right]. \] For any real number xi such that we have \[ lll xi & in & left[ sqrtfrac14+mu, \; 2 left vert k right vert^delta sqrtfrac14+mu right] , \] we denote by D_xi the disk centered at xi of radius 1/4. The Bessel function K_nu left( z right) being entire in nu for any positive real number z, the Cauchy formula gives \[ lll fracpartialpartial t_vert t \, = \, xi log K_t left( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right) & = & frac12ipi K_xi left( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right) \; int_partial D_xi \; fracK_nu left( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right)left( nu - xi right)^2 \; dnu . \] Using proposition , we get \[ scalemath0.96lll multicolumn3lfracpartialpartial t_vert t \, = \, xi log K_t left( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right) \\[0.5em] & = & frac12ipi \; fracK_1/2 left( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right)K_xi left( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right) \; int_partial D_xi \; frac1left( nu - xi right)^2 left( 1 + fracA_1 left( nu right)2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a + gamma_2 left( nu, 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right) right) dnu \\[0.5em] & = & fracK_1/2 left( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right)K_xi left( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right) \; left( fracxi2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a + O left( frac1left vert k right vert^2-4 delta a^2 right) right). \] For that last point, we have used the following estimate for the remainder gamma_2 \[ lllll left vert gamma_2 left( nu, 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right) right vert & leqslant & 2 left vert fracA_2 left( nu right)left( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right)^2 right vert exp left( fracleft( frac14+mu right) left vert k right vert^2 delta2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right) , \] which is uniformly bounded in k, but not in mu. Similarly, we have \[ scalemath0.96lll fracpartial^2partial t^2_vert t \, = \, xi log K_t left( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right) & = & fracK_1/2 left( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right)K_xi left( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right) left( 1 + O left( frac1left vert k right vert^2-4 delta right) right) , \] which means that we have, still on the same interval, \[ scalemath0.96lll widetildeF_mu,k left( t right) & = & fracK_1/2 left( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right)K_xi left( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right) cdot O left( frac1left vert k right vert^2-4 delta a^2 right) , \] with an implicit constant depending only on mu. The asymptotics of the modified Bessel function of the second kind show that the factor on the right-hand side is bounded on the interval we consider, uniformly in k. This concludes the proof.

We first note that the function $F_{\mu,k}$ has been defined so as to have
            
                \[ \begin{array}{lllll}
                        F_{\mu,k} \left( \pm \sqrt{\frac{1}{4}+\mu} \right) & = & F_{\mu,k}' \left( \pm \sqrt{\frac{1}{4}+\mu} \right) & = & 0
                    \end{array} . \]
            
                \noindent Since $F_{\mu,k}$ is holomorphic in $t$, it is of the form $F_{\mu,k} \left( t \right)= h_{\mu,k} \left( t^2 \right)$, where $h_{\mu,k}$ is holomorphic and such that we have
            
                \[ \begin{array}{lllll}
                        h_{\mu,k} \left( \frac{1}{4}+\mu \right) & = & h_{\mu,k}' \left( \frac{1}{4}+\mu \right) & = & 0
                    \end{array} . \]
            
                \noindent The Taylor-Lagrange theorem then allows us to write
            
                \[ \begin{array}{lllll}
                        F_{\mu,k} \left( t \right) & = & h_{\mu,k} \left( t^2 \right) & = & \frac{1}{2} \, \left( t^2 - \left( \frac{1}{4}+\mu \right) \right)^2 \; h_{\mu,k}'' \left( \xi_{\mu,t}^2 \right)
                    \end{array} , \]
            
                \noindent where $\xi_{\mu,t}$ is a real number with $\sqrt{1/4 + \mu} \leqslant \xi_{\mu,t} \leqslant 2 \left \vert k \right \vert^{\delta} \sqrt{1/4 + \mu}$. Note that we do not know how $\xi_{\mu,t}$ depends on $\mu$, $t$, or $k$. By differentiating $F_{\mu,k}$, we get
            
                \[ \begin{array}{lllclll}
                        F_{\mu,k}' \left( t \right) & = & 2t h_{\mu,k}' \left( t^2 \right), & & F_{\mu,k}'' \left( t \right) & = & 2 h_{\mu,k}' \left( t^2 \right) + 4t^2 h_{\mu,k}'' \left( t^2 \right)
                    \end{array} , \]
            
                \noindent and these two equalities can be combined to yield
            
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        h_{\mu,k}'' \left( t^2 \right) & = & \frac{1}{4t^2} \, F_{\mu,k}'' \left( t \right) - \frac{1}{4t^3} \, F_{\mu,k}' \left( t \right) \\[0.5em]
                    
                        & = & \frac{1}{4t^2} \, \frac{\partial^2}{\partial t^2} \log K_t \left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right) - \frac{1}{4t^3} \, \frac{\partial}{\partial t} \log K_t \left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right)
                    \end{array} \]
            
                \noindent Therefore, we have
            
                \[ \scalemath{0.98}{\begin{array}{lll}
                        F_{\mu,k} \left( t \right) & = & \left( t^2 - \left( \frac{1}{4}+\mu \right) \right)^2 \left[ \frac{1}{4\xi_{\mu,t}^2} \, \frac{\partial^2}{\partial t^2}_{\vert t \, = \, \xi_{\mu,t}} \log K_t \left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right) \right. \\[1em]
                    
                        && \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad - \left. \frac{1}{4\xi_{\mu,t}^3} \, \frac{\partial}{\partial t}_{\vert t \, = \, \xi_{\mu,t}} \log K_t \left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right) \right].
                    \end{array}} \]
            
                \noindent For any real number $\xi$ such that we have
            
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        \xi & \in & \left[ \sqrt{\frac{1}{4}+\mu}, \; 2 \left \vert k \right \vert^{\delta} \sqrt{\frac{1}{4}+\mu} \right]
                    \end{array} , \]
            
                \noindent we denote by $D_{\xi}$ the disk centered at $\xi$ of radius $1/4$. The Bessel function $K_{\nu} \left( z \right)$ being entire in $\nu$ for any positive real number $z$, the Cauchy formula gives
            
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        \frac{\partial}{\partial t}_{\vert t \, = \, \xi} \log K_t \left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right) & = & \frac{1}{2i\pi K_{\xi} \left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right)} \; \int_{\partial D_{\xi}} \; \frac{K_{\nu} \left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right)}{\left( \nu - \xi \right)^2} \; \text{d}\nu
                    \end{array} . \]
            
                \noindent Using proposition \ref{PropAsymptoticsModifiedBesselParameter}, we get
            
                \[ \scalemath{0.96}{\begin{array}{lll}
                        \multicolumn{3}{l}{\frac{\partial}{\partial t}_{\vert t \, = \, \xi} \log K_t \left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right)} \\[0.5em]
                    
                        \qquad & = & \frac{1}{2i\pi} \; \frac{K_{1/2} \left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right)}{K_{\xi} \left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right)} \; \int_{\partial D_{\xi}} \; \frac{1}{\left( \nu - \xi \right)^2} \left( 1 + \frac{A_1 \left( \nu \right)}{2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a} + \gamma_2 \left( \nu, 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right) \right) \text{d}\nu \\[0.5em]
                    
                        & = & \frac{K_{1/2} \left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right)}{K_{\xi} \left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right)} \; \left( \frac{\xi}{2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a} + O \left( \frac{1}{\left \vert k \right \vert^{2-4 \delta} a^2} \right) \right).
                    \end{array}} \]
            
                \noindent For that last point, we have used the following estimate for the remainder $\gamma_2$
            
                \[ \begin{array}{lllll}
                        \left \vert \gamma_2 \left( \nu, 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right) \right \vert & \leqslant & 2 \left \vert \frac{A_2 \left( \nu \right)}{\left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right)^2} \right \vert \exp \left( \frac{\left( \frac{1}{4}+\mu \right) \left \vert k \right \vert^{2 \delta}}{2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a} \right)
                    \end{array} , \]
            
                \noindent which is uniformly bounded in $k$, but not in $\mu$. Similarly, we have
            
                \[ \scalemath{0.96}{\begin{array}{lll}
                        \frac{\partial^2}{\partial t^2}_{\vert t \, = \, \xi} \log K_t \left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right) & = & \frac{K_{1/2} \left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right)}{K_{\xi} \left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right)} \left( 1 + O \left( \frac{1}{\left \vert k \right \vert^{2-4 \delta}} \right) \right)
                    \end{array}} , \]
            
                \noindent which means that we have, still on the same interval,
            
                \[ \scalemath{0.96}{\begin{array}{lll}
                        \widetilde{F}_{\mu,k} \left( t \right) & = & \frac{K_{1/2} \left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right)}{K_{\xi} \left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right)} \cdot O \left( \frac{1}{\left \vert k \right \vert^{2-4 \delta} a^2} \right)
                    \end{array}} , \]
            
                \noindent with an implicit constant depending only on $\mu$. The asymptotics of the modified Bessel function of the second kind show that the factor on the right-hand side is bounded on the interval we consider, uniformly in $k$. This concludes the proof.

                    \end{array} . \]
            
                \noindent For any such $\alpha$ and $\beta$, the dominated convergence theorem proves that the function

                    \end{array} \]

                    \end{array} \]

                    \end{array} \]

                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        \displaystyle s & \longmapsto & \displaystyle \sum\limits_{\left \vert k \right \vert \geqslant 1} \; B_{\mu,k} \left( s \right)
                    \end{array} \]
            
                \noindent is holomorphic around $0$, and we have

                    \end{array} \]

For any $k \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \left \{ 0 \right \}$ and any $\mu \geqslant 0$, proposition \ref{PropGlobalStudy} yields
                
                \[ \scalemath{0.97}{\begin{array}{lll}
                        \left \vert \left( \left \vert k \right \vert^{2 \delta} - \frac{1}{4} \right)^{-s} F_{\mu,k} \left( 2 \left \vert k \right \vert^{\delta} \sqrt{\frac{1}{4}+\mu} \right) \right \vert & \leqslant & \frac{C_{\mu}}{16 a^2 \left \vert k \right \vert^{2-4 \delta}} \left( \frac{1}{4} + \mu \right) \left( \left \vert k \right \vert^{2 \delta} - \frac{1}{4} \right)^{2 - \Re s}.
                    \end{array}} \]
            
                \noindent By the dominated convergence theorem, the sum of $A_{\mu,k}$ over non-zero integers is a holomorphic function on the half-plane $\Re s > 2 - 1 / \left( 4 \delta \right)$, and we can differentiate term by term. Evaluating the derivative of $A_{\mu,k}$ at $s \, = \, 0$ yields
            
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        \frac{\partial}{\partial s}_{\vert s \, = \, 0} \; A_{\mu,k} \left( s \right) & = & F_{\mu,k} \left( 2 \left \vert k \right \vert^{\delta} \sqrt{\frac{1}{4}+\mu} \right)
                    \end{array} , \]
            
                \noindent and we can set $\mu \, = \, 0$, to get the estimate
            
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        \displaystyle \left \vert \frac{\partial}{\partial s}_{\vert s \, = \, 0} \; A_{0,k} \left( s \right) \right \vert & \leqslant & \displaystyle \frac{1}{4} \; C_{0} \; \frac{1}{16 a^2} \cdot \frac{1}{\left \vert k \right \vert^{2 - 4 \delta}} \left( \left \vert k \right \vert^{2 \delta} - \frac{1}{4} \right)^2
                    \end{array} . \]
            
                \noindent This allows us to bound the derivative at $0$ of the series with general term $A_{0,k}$
            
                \[ \begin{array}{lllll}
                        \left \vert \frac{\partial}{\partial s}_{\vert s = 0} \; \sum\limits_{\left \vert k \right \vert \geqslant 1} \; A_{0,k} \left( s \right) \right \vert & \leqslant &  \frac{C_0}{4} \frac{1}{16 a^2} \; \sum\limits_{\left \vert k \right \vert \geqslant 1} \; \frac{1}{\left \vert k \right \vert^{2 - 4 \delta}} \left( \left \vert k \right \vert^{2 \delta} - \frac{1}{4} \right)^2
                    \end{array} . \]
            
                \noindent Since the series on the right hand side is absolutely convergent, we get
            
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        \frac{\partial}{\partial s}_{\vert s = 0} \; \sum\limits_{\left \vert k \right \vert \geqslant 1} \; A_{0,k} \left( s \right) & = & O \left( \frac{1}{a^2} \right).
                    \end{array} \]

nodes.statement: The key to this result is the bound given on widetildeeta_2 in corollary , whose notations will be used in this proof. For any non-zero integer k, we have \[ lllclll nu & = & left vert k right vert^delta sqrt4 mu + 1 & and & x nu & = & 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a . \] For k with large enough absolute value, say with left vert k right vert > K_0 the hypotheses of corollary are satisfied, and for such integers, we have \[ lll left vert widetildeeta_2 left( left vert k right vert^delta sqrt4 mu + 1, frac2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert aleft vert k right vert^delta sqrt4 mu + 1 right) right vert & leqslant & fracC4 pi^2 a^2 cdot frac1left( k + alpha right)^2 . \] The dominated convergence theorem proves that the function studied here is holomorphic on the half-plane Re s > - 1/left( 2 delta right). Its derivative at 0 is given by \[ l sumlimits_left vert k right vert geqslant 1 widetildeeta_2 left( left vert k right vert^delta sqrt4 mu + 1, frac2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert aleft vert k right vert^delta sqrt4 mu + 1 right) . \] To get the estimate on widetildeeta_2 for all non-zero integers, we will use corollary slightly differently. For any integer k > 0, we have \[ lllll multicolumn3lscriptstyle sqrtleft( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right)^2 + left( 4 mu + 1 right) left vert k right vert^2 delta & scriptstyle = & scriptstyle 2 pi a k sqrt left( 1 + fracalphak right)^2 + frac4 mu + 14 pi^2 a^2 cdot frac1k^2-2delta \\[1em] & = & multicolumn3lscriptstyle 2 pi a k left[ sqrt left( 1 + fracalphak right)^2 + frac4 mu + 14 pi^2 a^2 cdot frac1k^2-2delta - left( 1 + fracalphak + frac4 mu + 18 pi^2 a^2 cdot frac1k^2-2delta right) right] + 2 pi a k + 2 pi a alpha + frac4 mu + 14 pi a cdot frac1k^1-2delta. \] We further note that we have \[ ll multicolumn2lscriptstyle left vert sqrt left( 1 + fracalphak right)^2 + frac4 mu + 14 pi^2 a^2 cdot frac1k^2-2delta - left( 1 + fracalphak + frac4 mu + 18 pi^2 a^2 cdot frac1k^2-2delta right) right vert \\[1em] scriptstyle = & scriptstyle frac1sqrt left( 1 + fracalphak right)^2 + frac4 mu + 14 pi^2 a^2 cdot frac1k^2-2delta + 1 + fracalphak + frac4 mu + 18 pi^2 a^2 cdot frac1k^2-2delta left vert left( 1 + fracalphak right)^2 + frac4 mu + 14 pi^2 a^2 cdot frac1k^2-2delta - left( 1 + fracalphak + frac4 mu + 18 pi^2 a^2 cdot frac1k^2-2delta right)^2 right vert \\[1.5em] scriptstyle leqslant & scriptstyle fracleft( 4 mu + 1 right)^264 pi^4 a^4 cdot frac1k^4-2 delta + fracleft( 4 mu + 1 right) alpha4 pi^2 a2 cdot frac1k^3 - 2 delta, \] the last inequality being obtained after bounding the fraction by 1, and computing the difference. This proves that the function \[ lll s &longmapsto & sumlimits_k geqslant 1 k^1 - 2 delta s left[ sqrt left( 1 + fracalphak right)^2 + frac4 mu + 14 pi^2 a^2 cdot frac1k^2-2delta - left( 1 + fracalphak + frac4 mu + 18 pi^2 a^2 cdot frac1k^2-2delta right) right] \] is holomorphic on the half-plane Re s > 1 - 1/ left( 2 delta right), which contains the origin since we have delta < 1/2. For any complex number s with Re s > 1/delta, we have \[ lll multicolumn3lscriptstyle sumlimits_k geqslant 1 k^-2 delta s sqrtleft( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right)^2 + left( 4 mu + 1 right) left vert k right vert^2 delta \\[0.8em] & scriptstyle = & scriptstyle 2 pi a sumlimits_k geqslant 1 k^1 - 2 delta s left[ sqrt left( 1 + fracalphak right)^2 + frac4 mu + 14 pi^2 a^2 cdot frac1k^2-2delta - left( 1 + fracalphak + frac4 mu + 18 pi^2 a^2 cdot frac1k^2-2delta right) right] \\[0.8em] && scriptstyle + 2 pi a zeta left( 2 delta s - 1 right) + 2 pi a alpha zeta left( 2 delta s right) + frac4 mu + 14 pi a zeta left( 1 + 2 delta left( s - 1 right) right), \] and the associated function has a holomorphic continuation near the origin. The sum over integers k leqslant -1 can be dealt with similarly. After multiplication by the relevant factor, the derivative at s=0 is the one left uncomputed in the statement of the proposition. Let us move on to the term corresponding to j=1, which is \[ lll - s fracsin left(pi s right)4pi left( 4 mu + 1 right)^-s sumlimits_left vert k right vert geqslant 1 leftvert k right vert^-2 delta left( s+1 right) sqrtleft( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right)^2 + left( 4 mu + 1 right) left vert k right vert^2 delta . \] Using the same method as above, we have, on the half-plane Re s > 1/delta - 1, \[ lll multicolumn3l scriptstyle - s fracsin left(pi s right)4pi left( 4 mu + 1 right)^-s sumlimits_k geqslant 1 k^-2 delta left( s+1 right) sqrtleft( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right)^2 + left( 4 mu + 1 right) left vert k right vert^2 delta \\[1em] & scriptstyle = & scriptstyle - frac12 a s sin left( pi s right) left( 4 mu + 1 right)^-s sumlimits_k geqslant 1 k^1 - 2 delta left( s + 1 right) left( sqrt left( 1 + fracalphak right)^2 + frac4 mu + 14 pi^2 a^2 cdot frac1k^2-2delta - left( 1 + fracalphak + frac4 mu + 18 pi^2 a^2 cdot frac1k^2-2delta right) right) \\[1em] && scriptstyle - frac12 a s sin left( pi s right) left( 4 mu + 1 right)^-s left[ zeta left( 1 + 2 delta left( s+1 right) right) + alpha zeta left( 2 delta left( s+1 right) right) + frac4mu + 18 pi^2 a^2 zeta left( 1 + 2 delta s right) right]. \] Previously found estimates show that the first part on the right-hand side induces a holomorphic function on the half-plane Re s > - 1 / left( 2 delta right), whose derivative at 0 vanishes, due to the factor s sin left( pi s right). The Riemann zeta function having a unique pole, which is located at s=1 and simple, we note that the function \[ lll s & longmapsto & - frac12 a s sin left( pi s right) left( 4 mu + 1 right)^-s left[ zeta left( 1 + 2 delta left( s+1 right) right) + alpha zeta left( 2 delta left( s+1 right) right) right] \] is entire, and that its derivative at the origin vanishes. Similarly, the function \[ lll s & longmapsto & - frac12 a s sin left( pi s right) left( 4 mu + 1 right)^-s cdot frac4 mu + 18 pi^2 a ^2 zeta left( 1 + 2 delta s right) \] is entire, but its derivative at 0 does not vanish. We have \[ lll fracpartialpartial s_left vert s = 0 right. left[ - frac12 a s sin left( pi s right) left( 4 mu + 1 right)^-s cdot frac4 mu + 18 pi^2 a ^2 zeta left( 1 + 2 delta s right) right] & = & - frac18 pi a delta mu - frac132 pi a delta . \] One obtains similar results for the sum bearing over integers k leqslant -1. It only remains to study the remaining sum over integers j geqslant 2, given by \[ l - fracsin left( pi s right)pi left( 4 mu + 1 right)^-s sumlimits_j = 2^+ infty fracleft( s right)_jj! 4^j sumlimits_left vert k right vert geqslant 1 left vert k right vert^-2 delta left( s + j right) sqrtleft( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right)^2 + left( 4 mu + 1 right) left vert k right vert^2 delta . \] We only study the sum over integers k > 0, the other one being similar. We have \[ lll multicolumn3lscriptstyle sumlimits_j = 2^+ infty fracleft( s right)_jj! 4^j sumlimits_k geqslant 1 k^-2 delta left( s + j right) sqrtleft( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right)^2 + left( 4 mu + 1 right) k^2 delta \\[1em] & = & scriptstyle 2 pi a sumlimits_j = 2^+ infty fracleft( s right)_jj! 4^j sumlimits_k geqslant 1 k^1 - 2 delta left( s + j right) left[ sqrt left( 1 + fracalphak right)^2 + frac4 mu + 14 pi^2 a^2 cdot frac1k^2-2delta - left( 1 + fracalphak + frac4 mu + 18 pi^2 a^2 cdot frac1k^2-2delta right) right] \\[1em] && scriptstyle + 2 pi a sumlimits_j = 2^+ infty fracleft( s right)_jj! 4^j left[ zeta left( - 1 + 2 delta left( s+j right) right) + alpha zeta left( 2 delta left( s + j right) right) + frac4 mu + 18 pi^2 a^2 zeta left( 1 + 2 delta left( s + j - 1 right) right) right]. \] The first series on the right-hand side is holomorphic on Re s > -1 + 1/ left( 2 delta right), and, after multiplication by the appropriate factor, the derivative at s=0 vanishes, because of the Pochhammer symbols left( s right)_j. For the second part, the function \[ lll scriptstyle s & scriptstyle longmapsto & scriptstyle 2 pi a sumlimits_j = 2^+ infty fracleft( s right)_jj! 4^j left[ zeta left( - 1 + 2 delta left( s+j right) right) + alpha zeta left( 2 delta left( s + j right) right) + frac4 mu + 18 pi^2 a^2 zeta left( 1 + 2 delta left( s + j - 1 right) right) right] , \] is holomorphic around s=0, since 1/left( 2 delta right) is not an integer. Note that the function we study is indeed holomorphic on the half-plane $\Re s > 1/\delta$. The binomial formula (see proposition \ref{PropBinomialFormula}) then gives
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lllll}
                        \left( \left \vert k \right \vert^{2 \delta} - \frac{1}{4} \right)^{-s} & = & \left \vert k \right \vert^{-2 \delta s} \left( 1 - \frac{1}{4} \left \vert k \right \vert^{-2\delta} \right)^{-s}  & = & \sum\limits_{j = 0}^{+ \infty} \frac{1}{j! 4^{j}} \left( s \right)_j \left \vert k \right \vert^{-2 \delta \left( s + j \right)}
                    \end{array} . \]
                
                \noindent We can plug this into the function we study, and interchange both sums, to get
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        \multicolumn{3}{l}{\scriptstyle \sum\limits_{\left \vert k \right \vert \geqslant 1} \left( \left \vert k \right \vert^{2 \delta} - \frac{1}{4} \right)^{-s} \sqrt{\left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right)^2 + \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right) \left \vert k \right \vert^{2 \delta}}} \\[0.5em] 
                        
                        \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad & \scriptstyle = & \scriptstyle \sum\limits_{j = 0}^{+ \infty} \frac{1}{j! 4^{j}} \left( s \right)_j \sum\limits_{\left \vert k \right \vert \geqslant 1} \left \vert k \right \vert^{-2 \delta \left( s + j \right)} \sqrt{\left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right)^2 + \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right) \left \vert k \right \vert^{2 \delta}}.
                    \end{array} \]
                
                \noindent We will deal with the terms $j=0$ and $j=1$ separately, they are the only ones who contribute to the proposition. For any integer $k > 0$, we have
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lllll}
                        \multicolumn{3}{l}{\scriptstyle \sqrt{\left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right)^2 + \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right) \left \vert k \right \vert^{2 \delta}}} & \scriptstyle = & \scriptstyle 2 \pi a k \sqrt{ \left( 1 + \frac{\alpha}{k} \right)^2 + \frac{4 \mu + 1}{4 \pi^2 a^2} \cdot \frac{1}{k^{2-2\delta}}} \\[1em]
                        
                        \quad & = & \multicolumn{3}{l}{\scriptstyle 2 \pi a k \left[ \sqrt{ \left( 1 + \frac{\alpha}{k} \right)^2 + \frac{4 \mu + 1}{4 \pi^2 a^2} \cdot \frac{1}{k^{2-2\delta}}} - \left( 1 + \frac{\alpha}{k} + \frac{4 \mu + 1}{8 \pi^2 a^2} \cdot \frac{1}{k^{2-2\delta}} \right) \right] + 2 \pi a k + 2 \pi a \alpha + \frac{4 \mu + 1}{4 \pi a} \cdot \frac{1}{k^{1-2\delta}}}.
                    \end{array} \]
                
                \noindent We further note that we have
                
                \[ \begin{array}{ll}
                        \multicolumn{2}{l}{\scriptstyle \left \vert \sqrt{ \left( 1 + \frac{\alpha}{k} \right)^2 + \frac{4 \mu + 1}{4 \pi^2 a^2} \cdot \frac{1}{k^{2-2\delta}}} - \left( 1 + \frac{\alpha}{k} + \frac{4 \mu + 1}{8 \pi^2 a^2} \cdot \frac{1}{k^{2-2\delta}} \right) \right \vert} \\[1em]
                        
                        \scriptstyle = & \scriptstyle \frac{1}{\sqrt{ \left( 1 + \frac{\alpha}{k} \right)^2 + \frac{4 \mu + 1}{4 \pi^2 a^2} \cdot \frac{1}{k^{2-2\delta}}} + 1 + \frac{\alpha}{k} + \frac{4 \mu + 1}{8 \pi^2 a^2} \cdot \frac{1}{k^{2-2\delta}}} \left \vert \left( 1 + \frac{\alpha}{k} \right)^2 + \frac{4 \mu + 1}{4 \pi^2 a^2} \cdot \frac{1}{k^{2-2\delta}} - \left( 1 + \frac{\alpha}{k} + \frac{4 \mu + 1}{8 \pi^2 a^2} \cdot \frac{1}{k^{2-2\delta}} \right)^2 \right \vert \\[1.5em]
                        
                        \scriptstyle \leqslant & \scriptstyle \frac{\left( 4 \mu + 1 \right)^2}{64 \pi^4 a^4} \cdot \frac{1}{k^{4-2 \delta}} + \frac{\left( 4 \mu + 1 \right) \alpha}{4 \pi^2 a2} \cdot \frac{1}{k^{3 - 2 \delta}},
                    \end{array} \]
                
                \noindent the last inequality being obtained after bounding the fraction by $1$, and computing the difference. This proves that the function
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        s &\longmapsto & \sum\limits_{k \geqslant 1} k^{1 - 2 \delta s} \left[ \sqrt{ \left( 1 + \frac{\alpha}{k} \right)^2 + \frac{4 \mu + 1}{4 \pi^2 a^2} \cdot \frac{1}{k^{2-2\delta}}} - \left( 1 + \frac{\alpha}{k} + \frac{4 \mu + 1}{8 \pi^2 a^2} \cdot \frac{1}{k^{2-2\delta}} \right) \right]
                    \end{array} \]
                
                \noindent is holomorphic on the half-plane $\Re s > 1 - 1/ \left( 2 \delta \right)$, which contains the origin since we have $\delta < 1/2$. For any complex number $s$ with $\Re s > 1/\delta$, we have
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        \multicolumn{3}{l}{\scriptstyle \sum\limits_{k \geqslant 1} k^{-2 \delta s} \sqrt{\left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right)^2 + \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right) \left \vert k \right \vert^{2 \delta}}} \\[0.8em]
                        
                        \qquad \qquad & \scriptstyle = & \scriptstyle 2 \pi a \sum\limits_{k \geqslant 1} k^{1 - 2 \delta s} \left[ \sqrt{ \left( 1 + \frac{\alpha}{k} \right)^2 + \frac{4 \mu + 1}{4 \pi^2 a^2} \cdot \frac{1}{k^{2-2\delta}}} - \left( 1 + \frac{\alpha}{k} + \frac{4 \mu + 1}{8 \pi^2 a^2} \cdot \frac{1}{k^{2-2\delta}} \right) \right] \\[0.8em]
                        
                        && \scriptstyle \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad + 2 \pi a \zeta \left( 2 \delta s - 1 \right) + 2 \pi a \alpha \zeta \left( 2 \delta s \right) + \frac{4 \mu + 1}{4 \pi a} \zeta \left( 1 + 2 \delta \left( s - 1 \right) \right),
                    \end{array} \]
                
                \noindent and the associated function has a holomorphic continuation near the origin. The sum over integers $k \leqslant -1$ can be dealt with similarly. After multiplication by the relevant factor, the derivative at $s=0$ is the one left uncomputed in the statement of the proposition. Let us move on to the term corresponding to $j=1$, which is
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        - s \frac{\sin \left(\pi s \right)}{4\pi} \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right)^{-s} \sum\limits_{\left \vert k \right \vert \geqslant 1} \left\vert k \right \vert^{-2 \delta \left( s+1 \right)} \sqrt{\left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right)^2 + \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right) \left \vert k \right \vert^{2 \delta}}
                    \end{array} . \]
                
                \noindent Using the same method as above, we have, on the half-plane $\Re s > 1/\delta - 1$,
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        \multicolumn{3}{l}{ \scriptstyle - s \frac{\sin \left(\pi s \right)}{4\pi} \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right)^{-s} \sum\limits_{k \geqslant 1} k^{-2 \delta \left( s+1 \right)} \sqrt{\left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right)^2 + \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right) \left \vert k \right \vert^{2 \delta}}} \\[1em]
                        
                        & \scriptstyle = & \scriptstyle - \frac{1}{2} a s \sin \left( \pi s \right) \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right)^{-s} \sum\limits_{k \geqslant 1} k^{1 - 2 \delta \left( s + 1 \right)} \left( \sqrt{ \left( 1 + \frac{\alpha}{k} \right)^2 + \frac{4 \mu + 1}{4 \pi^2 a^2} \cdot \frac{1}{k^{2-2\delta}}} - \left( 1 + \frac{\alpha}{k} + \frac{4 \mu + 1}{8 \pi^2 a^2} \cdot \frac{1}{k^{2-2\delta}} \right) \right) \\[1em]
                        
                        && \qquad \scriptstyle - \frac{1}{2} a s \sin \left( \pi s \right) \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right)^{-s} \left[ \zeta \left( 1 + 2 \delta \left( s+1 \right) \right) + \alpha \zeta \left( 2 \delta \left( s+1 \right) \right) + \frac{4\mu + 1}{8 \pi^2 a^2} \zeta \left( 1 + 2 \delta s \right) \right].
                    \end{array} \]
                
                \noindent Previously found estimates show that the first part on the right-hand side induces a holomorphic function on the half-plane $\Re s > - 1 / \left( 2 \delta \right)$, whose derivative at $0$ vanishes, due to the factor $s \sin \left( \pi s \right)$. The Riemann zeta function having a unique pole, which is located at $s=1$ and simple, we note that the function
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        s & \longmapsto & - \frac{1}{2} a s \sin \left( \pi s \right) \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right)^{-s} \left[ \zeta \left( 1 + 2 \delta \left( s+1 \right) \right) + \alpha \zeta \left( 2 \delta \left( s+1 \right) \right) \right]
                    \end{array} \]
                
                \noindent is entire, and that its derivative at the origin vanishes. Similarly, the function
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        s & \longmapsto & - \frac{1}{2} a s \sin \left( \pi s \right) \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right)^{-s} \cdot \frac{4 \mu + 1}{8 \pi^2 a ^2} \zeta \left( 1 + 2 \delta s \right)
                    \end{array} \]
                
                \noindent is entire, but its derivative at $0$ does not vanish. We have
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        \frac{\partial}{\partial s}_{\left \vert s = 0 \right.} \left[ - \frac{1}{2} a s \sin \left( \pi s \right) \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right)^{-s} \cdot \frac{4 \mu + 1}{8 \pi^2 a ^2} \zeta \left( 1 + 2 \delta s \right) \right] & = & - \frac{1}{8 \pi a \delta} \mu - \frac{1}{32 \pi a \delta}
                    \end{array} . \]
                
                \noindent One obtains similar results for the sum bearing over integers $k \leqslant -1$. It only remains to study the remaining sum over integers $j \geqslant 2$, given by
                
                \[ \begin{array}{l}
                        - \frac{\sin \left( \pi s \right)}{\pi} \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right)^{-s} \sum\limits_{j = 2}^{+ \infty} \frac{\left( s \right)_j}{j! 4^{j}} \sum\limits_{\left \vert k \right \vert \geqslant 1} \left \vert k \right \vert^{-2 \delta \left( s + j \right)} \sqrt{\left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right)^2 + \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right) \left \vert k \right \vert^{2 \delta}}
                    \end{array} . \]
                
                \noindent We only study the sum over integers $k > 0$, the other one being similar. We have
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        \multicolumn{3}{l}{\scriptstyle \sum\limits_{j = 2}^{+ \infty} \frac{\left( s \right)_j}{j! 4^{j}} \sum\limits_{k \geqslant 1} k^{-2 \delta \left( s + j \right)} \sqrt{\left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right)^2 + \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right) k^{2 \delta}}} \\[1em]
                        
                        \qquad & = & \scriptstyle 2 \pi a \sum\limits_{j = 2}^{+ \infty} \frac{\left( s \right)_j}{j! 4^{j}} \sum\limits_{k \geqslant 1} k^{1 - 2 \delta \left( s + j \right)} \left[ \sqrt{ \left( 1 + \frac{\alpha}{k} \right)^2 + \frac{4 \mu + 1}{4 \pi^2 a^2} \cdot \frac{1}{k^{2-2\delta}}} - \left( 1 + \frac{\alpha}{k} + \frac{4 \mu + 1}{8 \pi^2 a^2} \cdot \frac{1}{k^{2-2\delta}} \right) \right] \\[1em]
                        
                        && \qquad \scriptstyle + 2 \pi a \sum\limits_{j = 2}^{+ \infty} \frac{\left( s \right)_j}{j! 4^{j}} \left[ \zeta \left( - 1 + 2 \delta \left( s+j \right) \right) + \alpha \zeta \left( 2 \delta \left( s + j \right) \right) + \frac{4 \mu + 1}{8 \pi^2 a^2} \zeta \left( 1 + 2 \delta \left( s + j - 1 \right) \right) \right].
                    \end{array} \]
                
                \noindent The first series on the right-hand side is holomorphic on $\Re s > -1 + 1/ \left( 2 \delta \right)$, and, after multiplication by the appropriate factor, the derivative at $s=0$ vanishes, because of the Pochhammer symbols $\left( s \right)_j$. For the second part, the function
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        \scriptstyle s & \scriptstyle \longmapsto & \scriptstyle 2 \pi a \sum\limits_{j = 2}^{+ \infty} \frac{\left( s \right)_j}{j! 4^{j}} \left[ \zeta \left( - 1 + 2 \delta \left( s+j \right) \right) + \alpha \zeta \left( 2 \delta \left( s + j \right) \right) + \frac{4 \mu + 1}{8 \pi^2 a^2} \zeta \left( 1 + 2 \delta \left( s + j - 1 \right) \right) \right]
                    \end{array} , \]
                
                \noindent is holomorphic around $s=0$, since $1/\left( 2 \delta \right)$ is not an integer. After multiplication by the relevant factor, the derivative at $s=0$ vanishes, because of the Pochhammer symbols. The sum over $k \leqslant -1$ is taken care of similarly, thus completing the proof.

Using Taylor's formula, we have, for every non-zero integer
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        \scriptstyle \mathrm{Arcsinh} \left( \frac{\left \vert k \right \vert^{\delta} \sqrt{4 \mu + 1}}{2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a} \right) & \scriptsize = & \scriptsize \frac{\left \vert k \right \vert^{\delta} \sqrt{4 \mu + 1}}{2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a} - \int_0^{\frac{\left \vert k \right \vert^{\delta} \sqrt{4 \mu + 1}}{2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a}} \frac{x}{\left( 1 + x^2 \right)^{3/2}} \left( \frac{\left \vert k \right \vert^{\delta} \sqrt{4 \mu + 1}}{2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a} - x \right) \mathrm{d}x
                    \end{array} . \]
                
                \noindent We further have the estimate
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        \scriptstyle \left \vert \int_0^{\frac{\left \vert k \right \vert^{\delta} \sqrt{4 \mu + 1}}{2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a}} \frac{x}{\left( 1 + x^2 \right)^{3/2}} \left( \frac{\left \vert k \right \vert^{\delta} \sqrt{4 \mu + 1}}{2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a} - x \right) \mathrm{d}x \right \vert & \scriptstyle \leqslant & \scriptstyle \frac{1}{2} \left( \frac{\left \vert k \right \vert^{\delta} \sqrt{4 \mu + 1}}{2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a} \right)^3
                    \end{array} . \]
                
                \noindent This proves that the function studied in this proposition is indeed holomorphic on the half-plane $\Re s > 1$. The binomial formula then gives
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        \scriptstyle \sum\limits_{\left \vert k \right \vert \geqslant 1} \left( \left \vert k \right \vert^{2 \delta} - \frac{1}{4} \right)^{-s} \left \vert k \right \vert^{\delta} \mathrm{Arcsinh} \left( \frac{\left \vert k \right \vert^{\delta} \sqrt{4 \mu + 1}}{2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a} \right) & \hspace{-1pt} \scriptstyle = \hspace{-1pt} & \scriptstyle \sum\limits_{j = 0}^{+ \infty} \frac{\left( s \right)_j}{j! 4^{j}} \sum\limits_{\left \vert k \right \vert \geqslant 1}  \left \vert k \right \vert^{-2 \delta \left( s + j \right) + \delta} \mathrm{Arcsinh} \left( \frac{\left \vert k \right \vert^{\delta} \sqrt{4 \mu + 1}}{2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a} \right).
                    \end{array} \]
                
                \noindent We will deal with the terms corresponding to $j=0$ and $j=1$ separately. We have
                
                \[ \begin{array}{ll}
                        \multicolumn{2}{l}{\scriptstyle \sum\limits_{\left \vert k \right \vert \geqslant 1}  \left \vert k \right \vert^{-2 \delta s + \delta} \mathrm{Arcsinh} \left( \frac{\left \vert k \right \vert^{\delta} \sqrt{4 \mu + 1}}{2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a} \right)} \\[0.6em]
                        
                        \scriptstyle = & \scriptstyle \frac{1}{2 \pi a} \sqrt{4 \mu + 1} \sum\limits_{\left \vert k \right \vert \geqslant 1} \frac{1}{\left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert} \left \vert k \right \vert^{-2 \delta s + 2 \delta} - \sum\limits_{\left \vert k \right \vert \geqslant 1}  \left \vert k \right \vert^{-2 \delta s + \delta} \int_0^{\frac{\left \vert k \right \vert^{\delta} \sqrt{4 \mu + 1}}{2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a}} \frac{x}{\left( 1 + x^2 \right)^{3/2}} \left( \frac{\left \vert k \right \vert^{\delta} \sqrt{4 \mu + 1}}{2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a} - x \right) \mathrm{d}x.
                    \end{array} \]
                
                \noindent The estimate already obtained on the integral proves that the second term on the right-hand side induces a holomorphic function on the half-plane $\Re s > 2 - 1/\delta$, which contains $0$ since we have $\delta < 1/2$. Let us study the first term. We have
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        \sum\limits_{\left \vert k \right \vert \geqslant 1} \frac{1}{\left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert} \left \vert k \right \vert^{-2 \delta s + 2 \delta} & = & 2 \zeta \left( 1 - 2 \delta + 2 \delta s \right) + 2 \sum\limits_{k \geqslant 1} \left[ \frac{1}{1 - \frac{\alpha^2}{k^2}} - 1 \right] k^{-1+2\delta - 2 \delta s}.
                    \end{array} \]
                
                \noindent Using the fact that we have
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        \left \vert \left[ \frac{1}{1 - \frac{\alpha^2}{k^2}} - 1 \right] k^{- 2 \delta s + 2 \delta} \right \vert & \leqslant & \frac{\alpha^2}{1 - \alpha^2} k^{- 3 + 2 \delta - 2 \delta \Re s}
                    \end{array} , \]
                
                \noindent and the continuation of the Riemann zeta function, the term we study has a holomorphic continuation near the origin. Its derivative there, after multiplication by the relevant factor, is uncomputed in the proposition. Similarly, we can take care of the term $j=1$, and find its contribution. The term corresponding to $j \geqslant 2$ is
                
                \[ \begin{array}{l}
                        \frac{\sin \left(\pi s \right)}{\pi} \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right)^{-s+1/2} \sum\limits_{j = 2}^{+ \infty} \frac{\left( s \right)_j}{j! 4^{j}} \sum\limits_{\left \vert k \right \vert \geqslant 1}  \left \vert k \right \vert^{-2 \delta \left( s + j \right) + \delta} \mathrm{Arcsinh} \left( \frac{\left \vert k \right \vert^{\delta} \sqrt{4 \mu + 1}}{2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a} \right)
                    \end{array} , \]

For any integer k geqslant 1, we have \[ llll multicolumn2lp left( frac2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert aleft vert k right vert^delta sqrt4 mu + 1 right) = & frack^delta sqrt4 mu + 12 pi left( k + alpha right) a + frack^delta sqrt4 mu + 12 pi left( k + alpha right) a left[ left( 1 + fracleft( 4 mu + 1 right) k^2 deltaleft( 2 pi left( k + alpha right) a right)^2 right)^-1/2 - 1 right] \\[1em] = & multicolumn3lfrack^delta sqrt4 mu + 12 pi left( k + alpha right) a - fracleft( 4 mu + 1 right) k^2 deltaleft( 2 pi left( k + alpha right) a right)^2 underbracescriptstyle left( 1 + fracleft( 4 mu + 1 right) k^2 deltaleft( 2 pi left( k + alpha right) a right)^2 right)^-1/2 left( 1 + left( 1 + fracleft( 4 mu + 1 right) k^2 deltaleft( 2 pi left( k + alpha right) a right)^2 right)^1/2 right)^-1_leqslant 1. \] In particular, the function \[ lll s & longmapsto & sumlimits_k geqslant 1 left( k^2 delta - frac14 right)^-s k^- delta frack^delta sqrt4 mu + 12 pi left( k + alpha right) a left[ left( 1 + fracleft( 4 mu + 1 right) k^2 deltaleft( 2 pi left( k + alpha right) a right)^2 right)^-1/2 - 1 right] \] is holomorphic on the half-plane Re s > left( delta - 1 right) / left( 2 delta right), which contains 0, having assumed that we have delta < 1. Let us now study the function \[ lll s & longmapsto & - fracsin left( pi s right)pi left( 4 mu + 1 right)^-s-1/2 sumlimits_k geqslant 1 left( k^2 delta - frac14 right)^-s k^-delta cdot frack^delta sqrt4 mu + 12 pi left( k + alpha right) a , \] which is well-defined and holomorphic and the half-plane Re s > 0. Using the binomial formula, which is the content of proposition , we have \[ lll multicolumn3l- fracsin left( pi s right)pi left( 4 mu + 1 right)^-s-1/2 sumlimits_k geqslant 1 left( k^2 delta - frac14 right)^-s k^-delta cdot frack^delta sqrt4 mu + 12 pi left( k + alpha right) a \\[1em] & = & - frac12 pi a fracsin left( pi s right)pi left( 4 mu + 1 right)^-s sumlimits_j = 0^+ infty fracleft( s right)_jj! 4^j sumlimits_k geqslant 1 k^-2 delta left( s + j right) frac1k + alpha. \] The sum over integers j geqslant 1 inducing a holomorphic function around 0, let us focus on the term corresponding to j=0, which is given by \[ lll multicolumn3l- frac12 pi a fracsin left( pi s right)pi left( 4 mu + 1 right)^-s sumlimits_k geqslant 1 k^-2 delta s frac1k + alpha \\[1em] & = & - frac12 pi a fracsin left( pi s right)pi left( 4 mu + 1 right)^-s Big( zeta left( 2 delta s + 1 right) + sumlimits_k geqslant 1 k^-2 delta s + 1 left( left( 1 + fracalphak right)^-1 - 1 right) Big). \] The second term above induces a holomorphic function around 0, as we have \[ lllll left vert left( 1 + fracalphak right)^-1 - 1 right vert & = & frac1k left( 1 + fracalphak right)^-1 & leqslant & frac1k . \] In the first term, the simple pole of zeta left( 2 delta s + 1 right) is canceled by the factor sin left( pi s right), and the result is holomorphic around the origin. Even though we only dealt with the sum over integers k geqslant 1, only small modifications are required for the sum over integers k leqslant -1, which is seen by switching the sign of alpha. This concludes the proof.

Recall that definition \ref{Defpxi} gives $p \left( x \right) = \left( 1+x^2 \right)^{-1/2}$ for all $x>0$. For any integer $k \geqslant 1$, we have
                
                \[ \begin{array}{llll}
                        \multicolumn{2}{l}{p \left( \frac{2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a}{\left \vert k \right \vert^{\delta} \sqrt{4 \mu + 1}} \right)} = & \frac{k^{\delta} \sqrt{4 \mu + 1}}{2 \pi \left( k + \alpha \right) a} + \frac{k^{\delta} \sqrt{4 \mu + 1}}{2 \pi \left( k + \alpha \right) a} \left[ \left( 1 + \frac{\left( 4 \mu + 1 \right) k^{2 \delta}}{\left( 2 \pi \left( k + \alpha \right) a \right)^2} \right)^{-1/2} - 1 \right] \\[1em]
                        
                        = & \multicolumn{3}{l}{\frac{k^{\delta} \sqrt{4 \mu + 1}}{2 \pi \left( k + \alpha \right) a} - \frac{\left( 4 \mu + 1 \right) k^{2 \delta}}{\left( 2 \pi \left( k + \alpha \right) a \right)^2} \underbrace{\scriptstyle \left( 1 + \frac{\left( 4 \mu + 1 \right) k^{2 \delta}}{\left( 2 \pi \left( k + \alpha \right) a \right)^2} \right)^{-1/2} \left( 1 + \left( 1 + \frac{\left( 4 \mu + 1 \right) k^{2 \delta}}{\left( 2 \pi \left( k + \alpha \right) a \right)^2} \right)^{1/2} \right)^{-1}}_{\leqslant 1}}.
                    \end{array} \]
                
                \noindent In particular, the function
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        s & \longmapsto & \sum\limits_{k \geqslant 1} \left( k^{2 \delta} - \frac{1}{4} \right)^{-s} k^{- \delta} \frac{k^{\delta} \sqrt{4 \mu + 1}}{2 \pi \left( k + \alpha \right) a} \left[ \left( 1 + \frac{\left( 4 \mu + 1 \right) k^{2 \delta}}{\left( 2 \pi \left( k + \alpha \right) a \right)^2} \right)^{-1/2} - 1 \right]
                    \end{array} \]
                
                \noindent is holomorphic on the half-plane $\Re s > \left( \delta - 1 \right) / \left( 2 \delta \right)$, which contains $0$, having assumed that we have $\delta < 1$. Let us now study the function
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        s & \longmapsto & - \frac{\sin \left( \pi s \right)}{\pi} \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right)^{-s-1/2} \sum\limits_{k \geqslant 1} \left( k^{2 \delta} - \frac{1}{4} \right)^{-s} k^{-\delta} \cdot \frac{k^{\delta} \sqrt{4 \mu + 1}}{2 \pi \left( k + \alpha \right) a}
                    \end{array} , \]
                
                \noindent which is well-defined and holomorphic and the half-plane $\Re s > 0$.  Using the binomial formula, which is the content of proposition \ref{PropBinomialFormula}, we have
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        \multicolumn{3}{l}{- \frac{\sin \left( \pi s \right)}{\pi} \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right)^{-s-1/2} \sum\limits_{k \geqslant 1} \left( k^{2 \delta} - \frac{1}{4} \right)^{-s} k^{-\delta} \cdot \frac{k^{\delta} \sqrt{4 \mu + 1}}{2 \pi \left( k + \alpha \right) a}} \\[1em]
                        
                        \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad & = & - \frac{1}{2 \pi a} \frac{\sin \left( \pi s \right)}{\pi} \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right)^{-s} \sum\limits_{j = 0}^{+ \infty} \frac{\left( s \right)_j}{j! 4^j} \sum\limits_{k \geqslant 1} k^{-2 \delta \left( s + j \right)} \frac{1}{k + \alpha}.
                    \end{array} \]
                
                \noindent The sum over integers $j \geqslant 1$ inducing a holomorphic function around $0$, let us focus on the term corresponding to $j=0$, which is given by
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        \multicolumn{3}{l}{- \frac{1}{2 \pi a} \frac{\sin \left( \pi s \right)}{\pi} \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right)^{-s} \sum\limits_{k \geqslant 1} k^{-2 \delta s} \frac{1}{k + \alpha}} \\[1em]
                        
                        \quad & = & - \frac{1}{2 \pi a} \frac{\sin \left( \pi s \right)}{\pi} \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right)^{-s} \Big( \zeta \left( 2 \delta s + 1 \right) + \sum\limits_{k \geqslant 1} k^{-2 \delta s + 1} \left( \left( 1 + \frac{\alpha}{k} \right)^{-1} - 1 \right) \Big).
                    \end{array} \]
                
                \noindent The second term above induces a holomorphic function around $0$, as we have
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lllll}
                        \left \vert \left( 1 + \frac{\alpha}{k} \right)^{-1} - 1 \right \vert & = & \frac{1}{k} \left( 1 + \frac{\alpha}{k} \right)^{-1} & \leqslant & \frac{1}{k}
                    \end{array} . \]
                
                 \noindent In the first term, the simple pole of $\zeta \left( 2 \delta s + 1 \right)$ is canceled by the factor $\sin \left( \pi s \right)$, and the result is holomorphic around the origin. Even though we only dealt with the sum over integers $k \geqslant 1$, only small modifications are required for the sum over integers $k \leqslant -1$, which is seen by switching the sign of $\alpha$. This concludes the proof.

nodes.name: Proof of proposition \ref{PropA7}
nodes.statement: We begin by noting that the function \[ lll s & longmapsto & sumlimits_left vert k right vert geqslant 1 left( left vert k right vert^2 delta - frac14 right)^-s sqrtleft( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right)^2 + frac14 + mu \] is indeed holomorphic on the half-plane Re s > 1 / delta. Though the existence of a holomorphic continuation can be proved using Taylor's formula, this method does not yield the mu-asymptotics of the derivative at 0. We will instead use the Ramanujan summation, which provides both results. Using the binomial formula, we get scalemath0.98lll multicolumn3lscriptstyle sumlimits_left vert k right vert geqslant 1 left( left vert k right vert^2 delta - frac14 right)^-s sqrtleft( 2 pi left vert k + alpha right vert a right)^2 + frac14 + mu \\[1em] & scriptstyle = & scriptstyle sumlimits_j = 0^+ infty fracleft( s right)_jj! 4^j Big[ sumlimits_k geqslant 1 k^-2 delta left( s + j right) sqrtleft( 2 pi left( k + alpha right) a right)^2 + frac14 + mu + sumlimits_k geqslant 1 k^-2 delta left( s + j right) sqrtleft( 2 pi left( k - alpha right) a right)^2 + frac14 + mu Big]. The sum has been split into two parts because there will be a small variation in the argument. We begin by dealing with the first part of , induced by \[ c sumlimits_k geqslant 1 k^-2 delta left( s + j right) sqrtleft( 2 pi left( k + alpha right) a right)^2 + frac14 + mu \] for every integer j geqslant 0. The first step in using the Ramanujan sumamtion is to find a function which interpolates, at integers, the general terms of the series we consider. We consider a fixed complex number s with Re s > 1 / delta, and set \[ lllll f_s,j & : & z & longmapsto & z^-2 delta left( s + j right) sqrtleft( 2 pi left( z + alpha right) a right)^2 + frac14 + mu , \] which is holomorphic on the half-plane Re z > 0, where we have denoted by sqrtcdot the principal branch of the complex square root. The function f_s,j is then of moderate growth, in the sense of definition . We now need to check that both hypotheses from theorem are satisfied. The first one, which is \[ lll limlimits_k rightarrow + infty f_s,j left( k right) & = & 0 \] holds, since we have Re s > 1 / delta. We now need to prove that we have \[ lll limlimits_k rightarrow + infty int_0^+ infty fracf_s,j left( k + i t right) - f_s,j left( k - i t right)e^2 pi t - 1 dt & = & 0 . \] The idea here is to use the dominated convergence theorem. In order to bound the function within the integral by an integrable one, we need to take some care with the denominator e^2 pi t - 1 at t = 0. We have \[ lll f_s,j left( k + i t right) & = & f_s,j left( k right) + i int_0^t f_s,j' left( k + ix right) dx, \\[0.5em] f_s,j left( k - i t right) & = & f_s,j left( k right) - i int_0^t f_s,j' left( k - ix right) dx, \] for any integer k geqslant 1 and any t in left] 0, + infty right[. Taking the difference then yields \[ lll f_s,j left( k + i t right) - f_s,j left( k - i t right) & = & i int_0^t left( f_s,j' left( k + ix right) + f_s,j' left( k - ix right) right) dx , \] giving an extra factor t which cancels the singular behavior of e^2 pi t - 1 at t = 0.                 \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        \scriptstyle s & \scriptstyle \longmapsto & \scriptstyle - \frac{\sin \left( \pi s \right)}{2 \pi} \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right)^{-s+1/2} \sum\limits_{\left \vert k \right \vert \geqslant 1} \left( \left \vert k \right \vert^{2 \delta}  - \frac{1}{4} \right)^{-s} \mathrm{Arcsinh} \left( \frac{\sqrt{1/4 + \mu}}{2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a} \right) \\[1em]

                    \end{array} \]

\label{PropR}
            
                The function
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        s & \longmapsto & \sum\limits_{\left \vert k \right \vert \geqslant 1} R_{\mu,k} \left( s \right)
                    \end{array} \]
                
                \noindent is holomorphic on the half-plane $\Re s > 1/\delta$, and has a holomorphic continuation to an open neighborhood of zero. Its derivative at $s = 0$ satisfies, as $\mu$ goes to infinity,
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        \multicolumn{3}{l}{\scriptstyle \frac{\partial}{\partial s}_{\left \vert s = 0 \right.} \left[ \sum\limits_{\left \vert k \right \vert \geqslant 1} R_{\mu,k} \left( s \right) \right]} \\[1em]
                        
                        & \scriptstyle = & \hspace{-3pt} \scriptstyle - \frac{\partial}{\partial s}_{\left \vert s = 0 \right.}  \left[ \frac{\sin \left( \pi s \right)}{\pi} \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right)^{-s} \left( - \sqrt{4 \mu + 1} \sum\limits_{\left \vert k \right \vert \geqslant 1} \left( \left \vert k \right \vert^{2 \delta} - \frac{1}{4} \right)^{- s + 1} \frac{\partial}{\partial t}_{\left \vert t = \sqrt{\frac{1}{4} + \mu} \right.} \log K_t \left( 2 \pi \left \vert k + \alpha \right \vert a \right) \right. \right. \\[1em]
                        
                        && \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \; \scriptstyle + \frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi}} \Gamma \left( \delta s \right) \Gamma \left( \frac{3}{2} - \delta s \right) \left( 4 \pi a \right)^{2 \delta s - 1} \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right)^{1 - \delta s} \cdot \frac{1}{\left( 2 \delta s - 1 \right) \left( 2 \delta s - 2 \right)} \\[1em]
                        
                        && \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \; \; \left. \left. \scriptstyle + \frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi}} \Gamma \left( \delta s \right) \Gamma \left( \frac{1}{2} - \delta s \right) 4^{\delta s - 1} \left( 2 \pi a \right)^{2 \delta s - 1} \left( 4 \mu + 1 \right)^{1 - \delta s} \cdot \frac{1}{2 \delta s - 1} \right) \right] \\[1em]
                        
                        && \scriptstyle + \frac{1}{4 \pi a} \left( 1 + \frac{1}{\delta} \right) \mu \log \mu - \frac{1}{4 \pi a \delta} \left( 1 + 2 \delta \log \left( 4 \pi a \right) + 3 \delta - 2 \log 2 \right) \mu  + \frac{1}{16 \pi a} \left( 1 + \frac{1}{\delta} \right) \log \mu \\[1em]
                        
                        && \qquad \scriptstyle - \frac{1}{8 \pi a} \log \left( 4 \pi a \right) + \frac{1}{8 \pi a \delta} \log 2 - \frac{1}{8 \pi a} + o \left( 1 \right).
                    \end{array} \]
                
                \noindent Furthermore, the same derivative, this time with $\mu = 0$, has the following asymptotic expansion, as $a$ goes to infinity,
                
                \[ \begin{array}{lll}
                        \frac{\partial}{\partial s}_{\left \vert s = 0 \right.} \left[ \sum\limits_{\left \vert k \right \vert \geqslant 1} R_{0,k} \left( s \right) \right] & = & o \left( 1 \right)
                    \end{array} . \]
